page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-80 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 80 vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES. The system is equipped with 320.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 75,092.52 and a PassMark CPU score of 52,649.44, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Memory subsystem performance is also strong, demonstrating read-only small block bandwidth of 4,129.09 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth of 94.1 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, as reflected by average-tier scores in Geekbench single-core (1,201.0) and stress-ng single-core tests. Software compilation with Clang is highly efficient, scoring 41,350.0 in Geekbench tests.

From a resource density perspective, the n2-standard-80 offers a balanced ratio of compute to memory, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that scale horizontally across many cores without requiring specialized memory-heavy configurations. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators presents a clear tradeoff, rendering it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated machine learning training or high-speed local disk caching. This is highlighted by its poor performance in large-model LLM text generation at 2.55 tokens/sec. The instance is best suited for multi-threaded CPU workloads, software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications.

It features a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Conversely, single-core metrics and large-model LLM text generation fall into average and poor tiers, respectively. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized, CPU-bound tasks that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. It is suited for software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
